models._description: (extension) UBL order import dispatch + EDI builder registration
(extension) product retrieval by variant ExtendedID (barcode / default_code)

behavioral_notes.observation: Outbound SELL-side builder: _export_order(sale_order) assembles a structured document_node via _get_sale_order_node then renders it with dict_to_xml(template=Order, nsmap=...) and returns UTF-8 bytes (etree.tostring, xml_declaration=True). _get_sale_order_node first prepares base lines from sale_order.order_line (non display_type) through account.tax._add_tax_details_in_base_lines / rounding helpers, forces item net prices positive ([BR-27]) and turns 'emptying' taxes into allowance/charge lines, then emits header (CustomizationID 'urn:fdc:peppol.eu:poacc:trns:order:3', ProfileID 'urn:fdc:peppol.eu:poacc:bis:ordering:3', cbc:ID = order name, IssueDate = create_date, OrderTypeCode '220', DocumentCurrencyCode, ValidityPeriod/EndDate = validity_date, OriginatorDocumentReference = client_order_ref), BuyerCustomerParty, SellerSupplierParty, Delivery, PaymentTerms, OrderLine items, AllowanceCharge (incl. early-payment-discount lines), TaxTotal and an AnticipatedMonetaryTotal. This whole Peppol BIS3 Order serialisation is pure Python and invisible in metadata.

Inbound dispatch (EXTENDS account/sale): _get_import_file_type sniffs file_data['xml_tree'] for CustomizationID == 'urn:fdc:peppol.eu:poacc:trns:order:3' and returns 'sale.edi.xml.ubl_bis3', else super(). _get_edi_decoder returns {'priority':20, 'decoder': sale.edi.xml.ubl_bis3._import_order_ubl} for that file type. _get_edi_builders appends self.env['sale.edi.xml.ubl_bis3'] to the (empty in core sale) list so the builder is offered on the portal/print 'Download Order' surface. So uploading/pasting a BIS3 order XML (or a PDF with embedded XML) into the sale order list routes it to this builder; the routing is code, not declarative config.

Override of the account base: calls super() then pops 'note' (the SO Terms & Conditions take precedence over the PO note), retrieves the BuyerCustomer partner via _import_partner (VAT / Peppol EAS+endpoint matching, create only with vat+name) into partner_id, sets client_order_ref = ID, origin = QuotationDocumentReference/ID, and a Delivery partner into partner_shipping_id. It imports document allowance/charges and lines from './{*}OrderLine/{*}LineItem' (_import_lines, tax_type='sale'), then adapts each line to sale.order.line: drops deferred_start/end_date and any discount, logs 'Could not retrieve the product named: ...' when no product matched, appends allowance/charge lines, and writes order_line as [Command.create(...)]. Returns (order_vals, logs); the parent _import_order_ubl writes them onto the order and posts a chatter note + a to-do activity listing the logs.

Override wraps the account base import: after super() fills the order, it takes order.order_line.filtered('product_id') and calls _compute_price_unit() then _compute_discount() on them. Effect: imported lines initially carry the XML-supplied price (discount stripped in _retrieve_order_vals), and this re-derives price_unit and discount from the company's own sale pricelist for matched products -- so the seller's pricing, not the buyer's PO price, governs the resulting quotation. A genuine side-effect chain invisible to metadata.

Model-adaptation layer between account.move.line and sale.order.line: _retrieve_line_vals renames the base 'quantity' key to 'product_uom_qty'. _get_product_xpaths adds variant_barcode (Item/StandardItemIdentification/ExtendedID) and variant_default_code (Item/SellersItemIdentification/ExtendedID) so product *variants* can be identified. product.product._get_product_domain_search_order / _get_retrieval_product_search_plan inject ExtendedID lookups (bisect.insort at priorities 12/14: default_code then barcode) so StandardItemIdentification.ID matches product.template.barcode while ExtendedID matches the product.product variant barcode. sale.order._get_line_vals_list builds extra lines at sequence 0 so they sort above the real order lines.

No OWL components, JS files, XML templates, registry adds or patches, and no asset bundles; extract_frontend reports present:false. The module is a headless EDI builder driven from the existing Sales UI (the sale order list 'Upload'/create-from-attachment flow and the portal/print Download-Order action exposed via _get_edi_builders). It defines no views of its own (views {} in facts).

it_architecture.application: sale_edi_ubl (Peppol BIS3 order EDI builder/importer for sale.order, extends account_edi_ubl_cii)
logical_data_erm: sale.edi.xml.ubl_bis3 -(matches)-> res.partner (BuyerCustomer / Delivery) and product.product (variant ExtendedID)
information_flows: side-effect: sale.order._export_order -> Peppol BIS3 Order XML bytes (download on portal/print)
side-effect: inbound BIS3 order XML/PDF -> _get_import_file_type -> _get_edi_decoder -> _import_order_ubl -> sale.order + sale.order.line (+ retrieve/create res.partner, match product.product)
side-effect: _import_order_ubl -> _compute_price_unit + _compute_discount re-derive seller pricing on imported lines (PO price discarded)
side-effect: _retrieve_order_vals drops the imported PO note so the SO Terms & Conditions win, and logs unmatched products as a to-do activity

capabilities: Export a sales order as a Peppol BIS Ordering 3 UBL document
Import an inbound BIS3 purchase-order XML/PDF into a sale.order (the seller side)
Retrieve-or-create the buyer and delivery partner from the order XML
Match ordered products (incl. variants via ExtendedID) to the catalog
Re-price imported order lines from the seller's own pricelist
value_streams: Outbound: confirmed/draft sale.order -> BIS3 UBL Order XML -> made available to the customer (portal/print download)
Inbound: customer's BIS3 order XML/PDF -> format detection -> sale.order with buyer/delivery partner, matched products and seller-derived pricing
information_concepts: sale.order (the order carried/created as a BIS3 UBL document)
res.partner (BuyerCustomer / Delivery party on the order)
product.product (ordered item, matched by ID / ExtendedID)
products: product.product (the ordered item matched from StandardItemIdentification / SellersItemIdentification, incl. variant ExtendedID)
policies: Order format fixed to Peppol BIS Ordering 3 (CustomizationID urn:fdc:peppol.eu:poacc:trns:order:3); routing keyed on that CustomizationID
Imported PO note discarded in favour of the SO Terms & Conditions
Imported line prices/discounts re-derived from the seller pricelist (PO price not trusted)
Item net price forced non-negative ([BR-27]); EN16931/PINT base-line rounding applied before serialisation
stakeholders: Seller / Salesperson (issues the BIS3 order acknowledgement / imports the customer PO)
Customer / Buyer (sends the BIS3 purchase order)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: sale_edi_ubl is the SELL-side electronic-ordering bridge: it serialises a sale.order into a Peppol BIS Ordering 3 UBL document and, inbound, turns a customer's BIS3 purchase-order XML/PDF into a sale.order (buyer/delivery partner retrieved, products matched, lines re-priced from the seller's pricelist). Unlike its parent account_edi_ubl_cii -- which is a support/compliance engine around account.move and classified 'support' / 9.0 Financial -- this module operates on the SALES ORDER document at order-capture time, advancing the quote-to-cash chain (it depends on 'sale', lives in category Sales/Sales, and reads/writes sale.order + sale.order.line, not invoices). That makes it a primary value-chain activity feeding APQC 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services (the order-management / 3.5 sales-order leg), specifically electronic order capture and acknowledgement. value_model 'chain' per Stabell & Fjeldstad: it progresses a linear order document rather than running a diagnostic loop (shop) or operating a mediating network. 9.0 Financial was rejected because the artefact is a sales order, not an invoice/ledger entry; the invoice-side EDI remains in account_edi_ubl_cii. It reuses the account_edi_ubl_cii UBL machinery (it _inherit's account.edi.xml.ubl_bis3) but applies it to the sell-side order, so the classification follows the sale order it serves.
classification.rationale_apqc_number: 3.0 number matches name 'Market and Sell Products and Services'; the invoice-EDI sibling sits at 9.0 Manage Financial Resources, deliberately not chosen here.

standard_capabilities: Export a sale.order as Peppol BIS Ordering 3 (UBL Order, OrderTypeCode 220)
Auto-detect inbound BIS3 order files from CustomizationID and import them into a sale.order
Retrieve-or-create buyer and delivery partners (VAT / Peppol EAS+endpoint matching)
Match products by StandardItemIdentification/SellersItemIdentification ID and variant ExtendedID
Re-derive imported line price_unit and discount from the seller's pricelist
Preserve the seller's Terms & Conditions over the buyer's PO note; log unmatched products as an activity
typical_fits: B2B / e-procurement where the customer sends a Peppol BIS3 purchase order and the seller wants it as a sale.order automatically
Returning a BIS3 order document/acknowledgement to a customer from the portal or print menu
Catalogs using product variants identified by ExtendedID (variant barcode / default_code)
Sellers who must re-price an incoming PO against their own pricelist rather than honour the PO price
common_gaps: Only Peppol BIS Ordering 3 is supported (no Order-Response, despatch advice, or other order CIUS/formats)
Actual Peppol Access Point transmission of the order (this module only builds/parses the XML; network delivery is a separate Peppol module)
Products that fail ID/ExtendedID matching are left without a product_id (logged) and need manual resolution
Imported PO pricing/discount is overwritten by the seller pricelist -- honouring buyer-agreed prices needs customisation
drive_hints: odoo shell: so = env['sale.order'].search([('state','!=','draft')], limit=1); xml = env['sale.edi.xml.ubl_bis3']._export_order(so); print(xml[:400])  # BIS3 Order XML head
UI: in the Sales order list use Upload / New-from-file with a BIS3 order XML (or a PDF carrying embedded XML) -> a sale.order is created with partner, lines and seller pricing

open_questions: Full set of EN16931/PINT business-rule constraints enforced on the order before serialisation (the export reuses the account.edi.xml.ubl_bis3 constraint layer; exact order-specific subset not enumerated here).
Precise buyer-vs-delivery partner matching precedence (Peppol EAS+endpoint vs VAT vs name) and the create threshold for a new res.partner on order import.
How an inbound order with no matched products is meant to be completed by the user (lines are created name-only with a to-do activity).
